headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/cascading-error from a prompt-leak source paired with an NLP consumer, but both are non-runnable docs-only profiles with no shared channel documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile B is explicitly about system prompt leaks, so it plausibly emits attacker-controlled prompt text. Profile A is an NLP resource with no runnable I/O surfaces or shared channel documented, so the bridge is not default. The pair risk exists mainly if an operator manually feeds B-derived text into A or another consumer.
conditions: IF an operator copies B-derived prompt text into A or a downstream NLP consumer
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added between the two profiles
mitigations: Keep the profiles isolated from any shared clipboard or workspace
Review any copied text from B before passing it to A
Tag B outputs as untrusted instructions
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to all inter-agent text transfers

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows data classes touched, shared workspace, or network egress. A is docs-only and non-runnable; B is also docs-only and non-runnable. With no documented sensitive data flow between them, there is no plausible leakage pathway in the current configuration.
conditions: IF either profile is later connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files
IF either profile is made runnable with file-reading permissions
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory
Do not grant file-reading permissions without review
Confirm both profiles remain non-runnable
requires-engineering: add access controls and audit logs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both profiles expose no write, filesystem, or network capabilities, and neither concurrency model nor mutable resource is documented. Without overlapping write surfaces, there is no capability conflict to arbitrate between A and B.
conditions: IF either profile gains write access to the same directory or mutable resource
IF an orchestrator later grants shared OAuth or git scopes
mitigations: Keep both profiles read-only
Avoid placing them under the same mutable workspace
Check for added write scopes before deployment
requires-engineering: introduce locking for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s prompt-leak theme can produce untrusted text, and A is an NLP-oriented resource that could be used to process such text. However, A is not runnable and no downstream action-taking authority is documented for either agent, so the cascade is limited to manual misuse rather than default automation.
conditions: IF B-generated text is treated as authoritative by a downstream system
IF A is inserted into a workflow that auto-acts on its outputs
mitigations: Require human review before acting on B-derived text
Mark B outputs as unverified
Do not auto-commit or auto-send based on A outputs
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either profile. A and B are both docs-only and touch no declared sensitive data, so there is no compliance mismatch evidenced in the pair.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later assigned to either profile
IF one profile is deployed under a residency or retention regime not shared by the other
mitigations: Document data-class handling before deployment
Verify residency and retention settings
Keep regulated data out of both profiles
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
